title: The Painter Lady vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: New homeowner comparing The Painter Lady and Precision Paint Experts? A plain-language guide to hiring your first painter in North Central Florida.
h1: The Painter Lady vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Just closed on a house and want it painted before the boxes are unpacked? Here is what first-time buyers should ask any painting contractor.

What should I ask a painter when hiring for the first time?

sections.h2: Hiring a painter for the first time
body: The Painter Lady is one of the painting companies North Central Florida homeowners may be comparing with Precision Paint Experts. We will not comment on any other business. This guide is written for new owners who have never hired a painter and are not sure what a good proposal looks like.

Buying a home tends to surface a list of small surprises: scuffed walls, patched holes, dated colors, maybe a popcorn ceiling. Painting is often the first project, and the empty-house window between closing and move-in is the easiest time to do it.

sections.h2: Five questions for every painter you call
body: Start by asking how a contractor protects the house: floors, fixtures, outlets, and any landscaping close to the walls. A new owner may not know which features are original or hard to replace, so the walkthrough is a good time to point out anything you want handled with extra care.
You do not need to know paint chemistry to compare bids. You do need these answers, in writing:
bullets: Are you licensed and insured in Florida, and do your workers carry workers' comp?
Which rooms and surfaces are included, and which are not?
What product line and how many coats?
When can you start, and how many days will it take?
What happens if something is not right at the end?

body: Precision Paint Experts is locally owned, with 15+ years of painting experience, and is licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida with workers' comp on every crew member. We use our own crews and do not subcontract.

A crew lead visits, measures, and writes an itemized estimate listing surfaces included and excluded, prep, primer and topcoat, coat count, and schedule. It usually arrives within one business day of the visit. No prices are published, because cost depends on measured area, condition, product line, access, and the number of colors. Most projects start one to three weeks after approval, so it helps to call shortly after your closing date is set.

sections.h2: Projects worth doing before the furniture arrives
body: An empty house makes some jobs much simpler. Ceiling painting and popcorn removal is far easier without furniture below, and our article on popcorn ceilings and asbestos explains the testing question to settle first. Wall patching through drywall repair and a full interior repaint can follow in the same visit. A whole-home interior typically takes three days to two weeks.
Already moved in? That works too. Crews move and protect furniture and work room by room, so you do not need to leave.

If you are thinking about the outside too, it can wait. Exteriors run best from October through May, and an interior project can be done in any season, so many new owners tackle the inside first and plan exterior painting for the following dry season.

Walkthroughs are usually scheduled within 48 hours. Anything not right at the final walkthrough is fixed before the job is closed out, and labelled touch-up paint stays with the house. Request your free estimate and compare it with any other quote you collect.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to paint a house I just bought?
faqs.a: We do not publish prices because cost depends on measured area, surface condition, product line, access, and colors. The free written estimate gives an itemized figure for your house.

faqs.q: Is it better to paint before or after moving in?
faqs.a: Before is simpler, especially for ceilings, but either works. If you are already in, crews move and protect furniture and work room by room.

faqs.q: Do I have to move out while the interior is painted?
faqs.a: No. Clients do not need to leave the home. Crews move and protect furniture and work room by room around you.
